label: R3
title: Review: Parts V and VI – verbs, saan/nasaan, time and ma-/maka-
summary: The book's review exercises on -um-, mag- and -in verbs, saan and nasaan, time words and telling the time, and ma- and maka- verbs, with the book's answers
goals: Give the five forms of -um-, mag- and -in verbs
Turn active sentences into passive ones with -in verbs
Translate time words and tell the time the Tagalog and the Spanish way
Use ma- and maka- verbs in the past

blocks.t: This lesson is the book's own **review exercises, Parts V and VI**. Every item is copied exactly as the book prints it. After each exercise you will find **the book's answer** from its answer key.

blocks.title: How to use this review
items: Say or write your own answer first. Then compare it with the book's answer.
Each exercise names the lesson to **revise** if you find it hard.
The exercises at the end of this lesson are built from the book's answers.
The exercise pages print few accent marks; the answer key prints more. Both are shown as printed.

sections.title: Part V A1. -um- and mag- verbs: the five forms

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Fill in the blanks with the **-um-** and **mag-** derivatives of the following words.
Remember from Lesson 14: each verb has five forms (infinitive, imperative, past, present and future). The infinitive and the imperative are the same.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
**takbó:** tumakbó (infinitive), tumakbó (imperative), tumakbó (past), tumatakbó (present), tátakbo (future)
**alís:** umalís, umalís, umalís, umaalís, áalis
**salitâ:** magsalitâ, magsalitâ, nagsalitâ, nagsasalitâ, magsásalitâ
**alagà:** mag-alagà, mag-alagà, nag-alagà, nag-aalagà, mag-áalagà

head: Form
takbó (-um-)
alís (-um-)
salitâ (mag-)
alagà (mag-)
blocks.title: The book's answer as a table
blocks.note: For -um- verbs the infinitive, imperative and past look the same. Mag- verbs use nag- for the past and present.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 14 (-um- and mag- verb forms).

sections.title: Part V A2. Translate into Tagalog

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Translate the following sentences into Tagalog.

head: English
rows: Peter and his friends left early.
Why didn't you clean your hands?
I want to buy two mangoes.
You should write to your mother every week.
He who studies well will speak Tagalog.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
a. Sumulat ng aklát si Mary.
b. Lumakad siya papunta sa páaralán.
c. Umalis nang maága si Peter at ang kanyang mga kaibigan.
d. Hindi makapaglutò si Mary ng kánin.
e. Bakit hindi ka naglínis ng mga kamáy?
f. Nagbebenta ba kayo ng mga manggá?
g. Gusto kong bumilí ng dalawáng manggá.
h. Mahúsay siyang bumasa.
i. Dapat kang sumúlat sa iyong ina linggú-linggó (or minsan sa isang linggo)
j. Kung sino ang nag-áaral nang mabuti ay magsásalitâ ng Tagalog.
k. Kumain ka ba ng almusál?
l. Umalis ba si Peter ngayóng umaga?
m. Ayaw mo bang lumangóy?

blocks.title: What else these answers use
items: **Dapat** and **gusto** are pseudo verbs (Lesson 17): the verb after them stays in the infinitive (sumúlat, bumilí).
**Ayaw** (*don't like*) is from Lesson 37: *Ayaw mo bang lumangóy?*
**Hindi makapaglutò** (cannot cook) shows being able to do something, like the maka- verbs (Lesson 18).
**Ba** comes after the pronouns **ka** and **mo**: *Kumain ka ba…?*, *Ayaw mo bang…?* (Lesson 10).

sections.title: Part V B1. -in verbs: the five forms

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Form the **-in** derivatives of the following words.

blocks.title: Book slips
items: The book prints *(to call)* under **sirain**. It belongs to **tawagin**: Lesson 15 gives sirain = *to break* and tawágin = *to call*.
The answer key gives no answer for **awitin**.
The answer key prints accents (dalhín, siráin, tawágin) that the exercise page leaves out.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
**sabihin:** sabihin (infinitive), sabihin (imperative), sinabi (past), sinasabi (present), sasabihin (future)
**dalhín:** dalhín, dalhín, dinala, dinadala, dadalhín
**siráin:** siráin, siráin, sinirà, sinisirà, sisirain
**tawágin:** tawágin, tawágin, tináwag, tinátawag, tatawagin

head: Form
sabihin
dalhín
siráin
tawágin
blocks.title: The book's answer as a table
blocks.note: Past: -in- is put in (in front of a vowel, or after the first consonant). Present: like the past, but the first syllable is doubled. Future: the first syllable is doubled, and -in/-hin goes on the end.

sections.title: Part V B2. Active into passive

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Change the following sentences from active into passive by using **-in** verbs.

head: Active (as printed)
rows: Sumulat siya sa akin ng liham.
Ang aking katulong ay nagluluto ng pagkain.
Bumati kayo kay Juan para sa akin.

blocks.t: Remember from Lesson 15: an **-in** verb is **passive**. The thing that receives the action becomes the subject, with **ang**, and the doer takes the **possessive form** (**ni Juan**, **ng aking katulong**, **nila**, **niya**). The verb comes first, then the doer, then the object.

blocks.title: Active → passive (item a)
blocks.note: Kumain sila ng isda. → Kinain nila ang isdâ.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
a. Kinain nila ang isdâ.
b. Sinulat niya ang liham sa akin.
c. Binabasa ni Juan ang pahayagan.
d. Niluluto ng aking katulong ang pagkain.
e. Sinabi ni Hesus ito.
f. Batiin ninyo si Juan para sa akin.
g. Minamahal mo ba ang Diyos?

blocks.title: Book spellings
items: Item e: the exercise prints **Jesus**; the answer prints **Hesus**.
Item a: the exercise prints **isda**; the answer prints **isdâ**.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 15 (-in- verb forms).

sections.title: Part V B3. Future tense with stress marks

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Give the future tense of the following active verbs and place the appropriate stress marks.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
a. bábasa
b. magdadalá
c. gigising
d. magbabago
e. maglalarô
f. magbábasâ
g. magsasabi
h. gágamot
i. áalis
j. mag-áalís

blocks.t: All of these repeat the first syllable of the root for the future. Look at **bábasa** (*will read*, an -um- verb) and **magbábasâ** (*will wet*, a mag- verb): the root basa / basâ is the same in spelling, but the stress and the affix tell them apart.

sections.title: Part V C. Saan and Nasaan

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** 1. When do you use **saan**? 2. When do you use **nasaan**? 3. Translate the following questions and sentences into Tagalog.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. **Saan** is used with an action word.
2. **Nasaan** is used without. Both ask for location.
3a. Nasaan ang iyong bahay?
3b. Nasaan ang iyong kaibigan?
3c. Saan pupunta ang iyong kaibigan?
3d. Nasaan ang iyong simbahan?
3e. Saan ka kumain?
3f. Si John ay nasa lungsod.

blocks.title: Saan + action, nasaan without
blocks.note: Where did you eat? · Where is your home?

blocks.title: Book spellings
blocks.t: Lesson 25 writes **násaán** (and nasaán). This review prints **nasaan** with no accents.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 25 (saán and násaán).

sections.title: Part V D. Find the wrong words

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Look for the wrong words in the following questions and sentence. If there are any, give the correct ones.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. (no error)
2. **Nasaan**
3. (no error)
4. **Nasa**
5. **Saan**

blocks.t: Use the rule from Part V C: item 2 has no action word, so **Saan** becomes **Nasaan**. Item 5 has an action word (pumaroón), so **Nasaan** becomes **Saan**. Item 4 tells where a person is (no action), so **Sa** becomes **Nasa**.

sections.title: Part VI A. Time words and telling the time

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Translate the following time, words and phrases.
Items 13 to 17 ask for each time in Tagalog; items 18 to 22 ask for the same times the Spanish way.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. ngayon · 2. bukas · 3. noong isang linggo · 4. kamakalawa · 5. kahapon · 6. sa isang taon
7. a while ago or earlier in the day · 8. later · 9. last January · 10. tomorrow afternoon · 11. on Sunday or next Sunday · 12. next year

head: Time
Tagalog
Spanish
rows: 21. alas diyes y medya ng umaga
22. alas dose y medya ng tanghali
blocks.title: The book's answer: telling the time
Book slips
items: Items 17 and 22 ask for **12:00 nn.**, but the answers add **at kalahati** and **y medya** (*and a half*), which is 12:30. For 12:00 noon Lesson 28 gives **ikalabindalawá ng tánghali** and **a las dose ng tánghali**.
Item 4 prints *day before*; the answer **kamakalawa** is the *day before yesterday* in Lesson 28.
Lesson 28 writes 2 o'clock as **ikalawá**; this answer key prints **ikadalawa**.
Lesson 28 writes the Spanish hours as **a las** (a las sinko); this answer key prints **alas**.
Lesson 28 prints kanína (*a moment ago*) and mámayâ (*later within the day*) with accents.

blocks.title: Revise
blocks.t: Revise: Lesson 28 (Telling time).

sections.title: Part VI B. Ma- and maka- verbs: the five forms

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Give the derivatives of the following words using the **ma-** and **maka-** affixes.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
**makaalis:** makaalis (infinitive), (none) (imperative), nakaalis (past), nakaaalis (present), makaaalis (future)
**makalakad:** makalakad, (none), nakalakad, nakalalakad, makalalakad
**matulog:** matulog, matulog, natulog, natutulog, matutulog

head: Form
makaalis
makalakad
matulog
blocks.title: The book's answer as a table
blocks.note: Past and present use na- / naka-. A maka- verb does not have an imperative form (Lesson 18).

blocks.title: Book spellings
blocks.t: The exercise prints **matúlog**; the answer key prints **matulog** with no accent.

sections.title: Part VI C. Translate into Tagalog

blocks.t: **Book's instruction:** Translate the following sentences into Tagalog

head: English
rows: He was able to buy shoes.
He was not able to pay.

blocks.title: The book's answer
items: Try it yourself first, then check your answers here.
1. Ano ang nakita mo kahapon?
2. Nakabili siya ng sapatos.
3. Natulog siya sa sahig.
4. Huwag kang magalit sa kanya.
5. Hindi siya nakabayad.
6. Nagising niya ang bata.

blocks.title: Spot the ma- and maka- verbs
items: **nakabili** (was able to buy) and **nakabayad** (was able to pay): maka- in the past.
**natulog** (slept): ma- in the past.
**Huwag kang magalit** (don't be angry): huwág + ka + ligature, then the verb (Lesson 37).
Item 6 asks for *the baby*; the book's answer uses **bata**.

exercises.q: Future of takbó (-um-), as the book prints it?
exercises.explain: Tumatakbó is the present; tumakbó is the infinitive, imperative and past.
Nagsalitâ is the past; magsásalitâ is the future.
Mag-alagà is the infinitive and imperative; nag-aalagà is the present.

exercises.en: Why didn't you clean your hands?
exercises.tl: Bakit hindi ka naglínis ng mga kamáy?

exercises.en: I want to buy two mangoes.
exercises.tl: Gusto kong bumilí ng dalawáng manggá.
exercises.explain: After gusto (a pseudo verb) the verb stays in the infinitive.
Tinátawag is the present; tatawagin is the future.
Dinala is the past; dadalhín is the future.

exercises.en: Passive of: Kumain sila ng isda.
Passive of: Bumabasa si Juan ng pahayagan.
Passive of: Nagmamahal ka ba sa Diyos?

Match the English to the book's future tense.

exercises.explain: The book: Saan is used with an action word. Nasaan is used without. Both ask for location.
Pupunta is an action word, so saan.

exercises.q: Saan ang iyong nanay? What does the book correct?
exercises.explain: There is no action word, so the book's answer is Nasaan.

exercises.q: Nasaan sila pumaroón? What does the book correct?
exercises.explain: Pumaroón is an action word, so the book's answer is Saan.

Match the Tagalog to the book's English.

options: alas diyes y medya ng umaga
exercises.answer: alas diyes y medya ng umaga
exercises.explain: Y medya = and a half. Alas otso kinse ng umaga is 8:15 a.m.

exercises.q: Imperative of makaalis in the book's answer?
exercises.explain: The book gives no imperative for makaalis or makalakad.
Nakalakad is the past; makalalakad is the future.

exercises.en: He was able to buy shoes.

recap: -um- verbs: tumakbó, tumakbó, tumakbó, tumatakbó, tátakbo. Mag- verbs: magsalitâ, nagsalitâ, nagsasalitâ, magsásalitâ.
-in verbs: tawágin, tináwag, tinátawag, tatawagin. Active → passive: Kumain sila ng isda. → Kinain nila ang isdâ.
Saan is used with an action word; nasaan without. Both ask for location.
Time: kanina, mamaya, noong Enero, bukas ng hapon; 10:30 a.m. = ikasampu at kalahati ng umaga = alas diyes y medya ng umaga.
Ma- and maka-: natulog (slept), nakabili (was able to buy), nakabayad (was able to pay).
